canonical_spec.title: Capital structure and financing frictions
canonical_spec.outcome: Compare financing policies under taxes, distress and incentive problems.

assignments.scope: Capital structure and financing frictions: derive financing irrelevance by equal total operating payoffs and replicable claims under explicit no-tax/no-cost/no-information/investment-feedback assumptions, then required-equity-return/leverage relation. Introduce corporate interest benefit and expected distress/issuance costs with compatible dated valuation; do not import a perpetual tax shield to a finite loan. Teach trade-off as conditional framework, information-based financing choices/pecking order as model predictions rather than universal ranks, agency risk shifting and debt overhang with a fully closed original state payoff example, rational creditor pricing and old versus newly priced debt. Separate stakeholder transfers from net value and expected bankruptcy costs from mere interest/principal. Address covenants/financing flexibility conceptually under fictional contracts; no unsupported current insolvency-law claims.

canonical_spec.title: Payout, liquidity and financial policy
canonical_spec.outcome: Choose payout and liquidity policies consistent with investment and constraints.

assignments.scope: Payout, liquidity and financial policy: derive benchmark dividend versus fair-price repurchase equivalence using pre/post-distribution equity value, shares outstanding and shareholder wealth; distinguish per-share mechanical effects/EPS accretion from value creation, price transfers when repurchase mispriced, and retained-cash opportunity cost. State investment policy and tax/transaction assumptions. Build original dated liquidity/working-capital/cash-buffer and committed-line case with uncertain needs, investment shortfall/covenant headroom, financing feedback and a coherent payout choice. Separate firm value, free cash and permitted/fundable cash. Explain information/signaling/agency motivations as conditional economic hypotheses. Use explicit hypothetical tax/contract rules rather than generic real legal payout assertions. Avoid pretending a higher dividend or buyback always benefits investors.

canonical_spec.title: Relative valuation and market evidence
canonical_spec.outcome: Use comparable valuations with economically meaningful denominators and peer choices.

assignments.scope: Relative valuation and market evidence: numerator/denominator consistency, operating EV versus equity and consolidated/excluded claims, market values and per-share units. Explain EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT, P/E and revenue/book multiples with applicability and negative/near-zero denominator limits. Derive a simple justified multiple from c03 stable cash/reinvestment economics to show risk/growth/margin/capital-intensity effects. Original peer dataset with provenance as fictional inputs, explicitly matched dates/forward versus trailing periods, normalization of recurring/transitory earnings and cycle effects without cherry picking; account for debt, leases and noncontrolling claims consistently. Median/range/weighted aggregation distinctions, comparable selection and defensible exclusions, transaction/control differences and DCF triangulation. Quantify a misleading apparent cheapness or EPS/multiple mismatch; no actual current market claims.

canonical_spec.title: Real options and investment timing
canonical_spec.outcome: Value flexibility and identify where static NPV understates contingent choices.

assignments.scope: Real options and investment timing: define feasible rights, irreversible investment and lost operating opportunities; derive backward induction using explicit compatible valuation at each chance node and maximization only after information available. Value original delay, expansion, abandonment and staged-investment cases; distinguish flexible versus fixed policy, value of information versus option/ownership costs, and avoid double-counting flexibility in both forecast and premium. Provide a simple replication-priced binomial case with the exact spanning/no-arbitrage/currency/timing assumptions taught locally; physical probabilities are for forecasts and information decisions, not freely interchanged with risk-neutral valuation weights. Nontradable project uncertainty requires a justified preference/pricing rule, not automatic Black-Scholes or risk-free discounting of physical means. Teach timing, expiry, competition/funding constraints and sensitivity; complete original lab and all eight solutions.
